schema_info.description: One row per schema version applied to this database, recording which version of the relational model the file carries and when it was installed.

schema_version.description: Version label of the applied schema. Agrees with the header of schema/schema.sql, this table's seeded row, and PRAGMA user_version; a check enforces that all three match.

applied_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME applied this schema version to the database. An audit time, not an observation time from the research data.

description.description: Free-text note shipped alongside the schema version seed, summarizing what changed in that version.

projects.description: A research project: the outermost scope that owns recordings, experimental entities, source files, and the configuration profiles under which their source material is interpreted.

project_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the project, generated by the database and meaningful only inside this file.

project_key.description: Caller-supplied stable identifier for the project, unique within the database and declared explicitly at intake rather than inferred from the source hierarchy. This is the project's durable identity, so it survives a database rebuild in a way project_id does not.

project_name.description: Human-readable name for the project, used when reporting results to a person.

description.description: Free-text account of what the project covers. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

created_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME created this row. An audit time, not a fact about when the research took place.

archived_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when the project was archived. Null while the project is still active.

config_profiles.description: A named configuration profile: one interpretation contract, such as how a project's directory structure is read or how an extractor's output columns are understood. Rows elsewhere cite a profile version to record the assumptions under which they were produced.

profile_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the configuration profile, generated by the database.

project_id.description: Project that owns this profile. Null for a profile shipped with VAWLUME, which is available to every project in the database.

profile_key.description: Stable identifier for the profile, supplied by the profile document rather than generated. Together with the profile kind it forms the profile's durable identity, and it is unique within its project.

profile_name.description: Human-readable name for the profile, used when reporting which configuration produced a result.

profile_kind.description: Which interpretation contract this profile expresses, drawn from a declared vocabulary that separates source and project mapping, extractor output and settings, recording device, experimental setup, tracking and attribution input mapping, analysis settings, and policy. The kinds are deliberately distinct so that one profile cannot silently take on another's responsibility.

is_builtin.description: Whether VAWLUME shipped this profile (1) or a user authored it (0). Built-in profiles are seeded from the repository rather than registered from a user document.

description.description: Free-text account of what the profile interprets and under what assumptions. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

created_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME created this row. An audit time, not a property of the profile document.

config_profile_versions.description: One registered version of a configuration profile, carrying where its document was read from and a digest of its contents, so that any row citing this version can be traced back to the exact document that was in force when it was written.

profile_version_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this profile version, generated by the database. This is what other tables cite when they record which configuration governed them.

profile_id.description: Configuration profile that this is a version of.

version_label.description: Version as authored in the profile document itself. Unique within its profile and part of the version's durable identity, so republishing changed content under an existing label is refused rather than accepted.

profile_schema_version.description: Which revision of the profile document grammar this version was written against, as distinct from the version of the profile's own content. Null when the document declares none.

content_format.description: Serialization of the registered document, normally inferred from its file extension. VAWLUME's own configuration is JSON; the other permitted values exist so an externally authored document can be registered and cited without first being rewritten.

content_uri.description: Where the profile document was read from, stored repository-relative when the file lives under the repository root and absolute otherwise. The file is hashed, never copied, so this records a location rather than custody of the bytes.

checksum_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the profile document as registered. Re-registering this same version label over different bytes is reported as a conflict, because rows already cite this version by identifier and changing what it denotes would silently re-point their provenance.

is_snapshot.description: Caller-declared flag recording whether the registered content is a fixed snapshot rather than a reference expected to change underneath it. Defaults to true and is a statement about the document, not something VAWLUME verifies.

created_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME registered this version. An audit time, not the date the profile was authored.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about this particular version. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

project_profile_assignments.description: Records that a configuration profile version applies to a project in a named role, which is how a project declares the defaults its recordings can inherit.

project_id.description: Project the profile version is assigned to.

profile_version_id.description: Exact profile version being assigned. A version, not a profile, so the assignment records which content was in force.

assignment_role.description: The role this profile version plays for the project. The same version can be assigned in more than one role, so the role is part of the assignment's identity rather than a label on it.

is_default.description: Whether this assignment is the project default for its role, and therefore a candidate for inheritance onto recordings that declare no assignment of their own.

assigned_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME created this assignment. An audit time.

source_files.description: A file VAWLUME discovered and registered as project source material, identified by its location within the project rather than by its absolute runtime path, so that relocating a project root reuses the same rows.

source_file_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the registered file, generated by the database.

project_id.description: Project this file was discovered within.

file_role.description: What this file is to the project, such as the audio a recording was made from or an artifact an extractor produced. It records how the file was claimed rather than what format it happens to be.

path_or_uri.description: Location the file was discovered at, as discovered, and unique within its project. Absolute runtime paths are used to prove a file exists for one execution and are deliberately not what intake treats as identity.

relative_path.description: Normalized portable path of the file within the project root. Together with the project this is what intake treats as the file's durable identity, which is why relocating a project root reuses the same rows rather than registering the files again.

filename.description: Base name of the file, separated out so that files sharing a name in different folders remain distinguishable while still being searchable by name.

file_format.description: Format of the file as recorded at discovery, normally derived from its extension. Not verified by reading the file.

size_bytes.description: Size of the file in bytes at discovery. Null when discovery did not record it.

checksum_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file's contents at registration. Relocating the file is recognised as the same file; a change to its contents is a conflict rather than an overwrite. Null when no digest was taken.

source_modified_at.description: Modification time as reported by the source, in whatever form the source expressed it. Deliberately not recorded as UTC: VAWLUME does not know the zone it was expressed in and will not assert one.

discovered_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME registered this file. An audit time, and distinct from the file's own modification time.

ingestion_runs.description: One attempt to ingest a project's source material under a particular mapping profile version. Successful reruns create new rows rather than rewriting earlier ones, so the history of attempts survives even when the resulting graph is unchanged.

ingestion_run_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this ingestion attempt, generated by the database.

mapping_profile_version_id.description: Exact project-input mapping profile version that interpreted the sources for this attempt. This is what makes the resulting rows traceable to the rules that produced them.

run_label.description: Optional caller-supplied label distinguishing this attempt from others. Free text with no uniqueness requirement.

vawlume_version.description: Version of VAWLUME the caller asserted was in use. Supplied by the caller and never inferred from the working tree, so it records a claim rather than a verified fact.

source_commit.description: Source revision the caller asserted was in use. Like the version, a caller claim that VAWLUME records without checking.

status.description: State of the attempt, drawn from a declared vocabulary that separates one still in progress from one that completed, one that completed with warnings, and one that failed. Warnings are not errors and the distinction is kept.

started_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when the attempt began.

completed_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when the attempt finished. Null while the attempt is unfinished or if it never reached a terminal state.

log_uri.description: Location of an external log for this attempt, when the caller recorded one. VAWLUME stores the reference and does not read it.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about this attempt. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

ingestion_files.description: Records how one source file fared in one ingestion attempt, so that a run's outcome can be read per file rather than only in aggregate.

ingestion_run_id.description: Ingestion attempt this outcome belongs to.

source_file_id.description: Source file this outcome is about.

parse_status.description: How this file fared in this attempt, drawn from a declared vocabulary that separates a file not yet reached, a clean parse, a parse with warnings, a file deliberately skipped, and a failure. Skipped and failed are different outcomes and are kept apart.

warning_count.description: Number of warnings raised while parsing this file in this attempt. Zero means none were raised, not that none were possible.

error_count.description: Number of errors raised while parsing this file in this attempt.

parser_message.description: Human-readable summary of what the parser reported for this file. Diagnostic text, not a structured issue record.

entity_types.description: One level of a project's own experimental hierarchy, such as its notion of a cohort, a subject, or a session, registered under the project's native name for it and optionally mapped to a canonical role VAWLUME understands.

entity_type_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this hierarchy level, generated by the database.

project_id.description: Project whose hierarchy this level belongs to. Levels are project-scoped because two projects may use the same word for different things.

native_name.description: The project's own name for this level, preserved as the source expressed it. Unique within the project and part of the level's durable identity.

canonical_role.description: The role this level is declared to fill, such as a study, a subject, or a session. An open vocabulary rather than a fixed one, so a project can declare a role VAWLUME does not model natively. This is the added canonical reading; the native name remains the source's own. Null when no canonical role was declared.

hierarchy_order.description: Where this level sits in the project's declared nesting, as the project ordered it. VAWLUME stores the ordering and neither computes nor enforces it. Null when the project declared no ordering.

is_biological_unit.description: Whether entities at this level are biological individuals rather than organizational groupings. Declared by the project, not inferred from the level's name.

is_subject_like.description: Whether entities at this level behave as subjects for analysis purposes. Kept separate from the biological flag because the two can disagree: an organizational unit may be analysed as a subject, and a biological individual may not be the unit of analysis.

description.description: Free-text account of what this level represents in the project. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

experimental_entities.description: One thing in a project's experimental hierarchy — a particular cohort, subject, or session — identified by the project's own name for it at its own level.

entity_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this entity, generated by the database.

entity_type_id.description: Hierarchy level this entity sits at, which is what makes its native identifier interpretable.

native_id.description: The project's own identifier for this entity, preserved as the source expressed it. Unique within its level, and together with the level it forms the entity's durable identity.

display_label.description: Human-readable label for the entity when the native identifier is not itself readable. Null when none was supplied.

ingestion_run_id.description: Ingestion attempt that first created this row. Later compatible attempts record their own audit rows rather than rewriting this provenance, so this names the attempt the entity entered the database on.

created_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME created this row. An audit time, not a fact about the experiment.

entity_relationships.description: A declared relationship between two entities in a project's hierarchy, most often containment, together with the source evidence and mapping rule that produced it. An entity may not be related to itself.

entity_relationship_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this relationship, generated by the database.

parent_entity_id.description: The containing or superior entity of the pair. Which endpoint is the parent is part of the relationship's meaning, not an arbitrary ordering.

child_entity_id.description: The contained or subordinate entity of the pair, and never the same entity as the parent.

relationship_type.description: What the relationship asserts between the two endpoints, defaulting to containment. Free text so a project can declare a relationship VAWLUME does not model natively.

role_label.description: The role the child plays in this relationship when the type alone is not specific enough. Part of the relationship's durable identity, so the same pair can be related more than once in different roles.

valid_from_utc.description: UTC time from which this relationship is asserted to hold. Null when the relationship is not time-bounded at its start.

valid_to_utc.description: UTC time until which this relationship is asserted to hold. Null when the relationship is open-ended.

ingestion_run_id.description: Ingestion attempt that first created this row. Null when the relationship did not arise from an ingestion attempt.

source_file_id.description: Source file this relationship was read from, when it came from one. Null when the relationship has no single originating file.

source_locator.description: Where within the source this relationship was read from, recorded so the assertion can be traced back to the text that produced it.

mapping_rule_key.description: Which rule in the mapping profile claimed this relationship, so the interpretation is traceable to the rule that made it rather than only to the profile as a whole.

entity_attributes.description: One attribute of one entity, stored in a typed column chosen by its declared value type, together with the source location and mapping rule it came from. Values reach this table because a mapping rule claimed them as attributes, not because they appeared in a source file.

entity_attribute_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this attribute row, generated by the database.

attribute_name.description: The attribute's name as the source expressed it, preserved rather than normalized.

value_type.description: Which of the typed value columns carries this attribute's value, or the declared absence of a value. A constraint enforces that exactly one typed column is populated, and that none is when the value is absent, so a missing value can never be confused with an empty one.

value_text.description: The attribute's value when it is textual, and null otherwise.

value_real.description: The attribute's value when it is a real number, and null otherwise.

value_integer.description: The attribute's value when it is an integer, and null otherwise.

value_boolean.description: The attribute's value when it is a truth value, stored as 0 or 1, and null otherwise.

value_json.description: The attribute's value when it is a structured payload, stored as JSON text, and null otherwise.

unit.description: Unit the source expressed the value in, as the source expressed it. Free text that VAWLUME records and never interprets or converts.

ingestion_run_id.description: Ingestion attempt that first created this row. Null when the attribute did not arise from an ingestion attempt.

source_file_id.description: Source file this attribute was read from, when it came from one.

source_locator.description: Where within the source this value was read from, recorded so it can be traced back to the text it came from.

mapping_rule_key.description: Which rule in the mapping profile claimed this value, so the interpretation is traceable to the rule that made it.

recordings.description: One audio recording, anchored to exactly one registered source file. That anchor is the boundary extractor imports resolve against, so a recording is identified by the file it was made from rather than by any name an extractor gives it.

recording_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the recording, generated by the database.

source_file_id.description: The registered audio file this recording is made from, unique across recordings. This one-to-one anchor is the recording's durable identity and the point extractor importers attach their runs to.

native_recording_id.description: The source's own identifier for this recording, preserved as expressed. Null when the source names recordings only by filename.

checksum_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the audio as registered. Null in the ordinary case, because intake does not open audio files; it is populated only when some adapter supplied the digest.

sample_rate_hz.description: Sampling rate in hertz, when it is known. Null in the ordinary case: intake reads no audio metadata, so this is populated only when an adapter supplied it rather than being measured from the file.

bit_depth.description: Bits per sample, when it is known. Like the sampling rate, supplied rather than measured, and null when nothing supplied it.

channel_count.description: Number of channels the recording is declared to have, when it is known. Supplied rather than measured. A declared channel index above this count is refused; a recording declaring no count is not checked at all.

duration_s.description: Duration in seconds, when it is known. Supplied rather than measured, and null in the ordinary case.

recorded_start_utc.description: UTC time the recording is asserted to have started. An assertion about the world, unlike the audit timestamp on this row, and null when nothing asserted it.

created_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME created this row. An audit time, and not to be read as when the recording was made.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the recording. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

recording_channels.description: One channel of one recording. A channel row is a caller assertion that the recording has that channel; nothing inspects the audio to confirm it, and the microphone that produced it is placed in space by a separate row.

recording_channel_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this channel, generated by the database.

recording_id.description: Recording this channel belongs to. A channel belongs to exactly one recording, which is what makes anything attached to it session-specific.

channel_index.description: Position of this channel within the recording, counting from one, and unique within the recording. Refused when it exceeds a declared channel count.

channel_label.description: Human-readable label for the channel as the source named it. Null when the source named it only by index.

channel_role.description: What this channel is for, when the caller declared a role for it. Free text, and null when no role was declared.

recording_entity_links.description: Records that an entity took part in a recording in a named role, optionally over a bounded interval within it. This is how the experimental hierarchy reaches individual recordings.

recording_entity_link_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this participation record, generated by the database.

recording_id.description: Recording the entity took part in.

link_type.description: The nature of the entity's involvement, defaulting to participation. Free text so a project can declare an involvement VAWLUME does not model natively, and part of the link's durable identity.

role_label.description: The role the entity played, when the link type alone is not specific enough. Part of the link's durable identity, so one entity can be linked to one recording more than once in different roles.

start_time_s.description: Seconds from the start of the recording at which the entity's involvement begins. Null when the involvement is not time-bounded, which is the ordinary case for a participant present throughout.

end_time_s.description: Seconds from the start of the recording at which the entity's involvement ends, never before the start. Null when the involvement is open-ended.

ingestion_run_id.description: Ingestion attempt that first created this row. Null when the link did not arise from an ingestion attempt.

recording_attributes.description: One attribute of one recording, stored in a typed column chosen by its declared value type, together with the source location and mapping rule it came from. The same typed-value shape as entity attributes, scoped to a recording rather than to a participant in the hierarchy.

recording_attribute_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this attribute row, generated by the database.

recording_id.description: Recording this attribute describes.

attribute_name.description: The attribute's name as the source expressed it, preserved rather than normalized.

value_type.description: Which of the typed value columns carries this attribute's value, or the declared absence of a value. A constraint enforces that exactly one typed column is populated, and that none is when the value is absent, so a missing value can never be confused with an empty one.

value_text.description: The attribute's value when it is textual, and null otherwise.

value_real.description: The attribute's value when it is a real number, and null otherwise.

value_integer.description: The attribute's value when it is an integer, and null otherwise.

value_boolean.description: The attribute's value when it is a truth value, stored as 0 or 1, and null otherwise.

value_json.description: The attribute's value when it is a structured payload, stored as JSON text, and null otherwise.

unit.description: Unit the source expressed the value in, as the source expressed it. Free text that VAWLUME records and never interprets or converts.

ingestion_run_id.description: Ingestion attempt that first created this row. Null when the attribute did not arise from an ingestion attempt.

source_file_id.description: Source file this attribute was read from, when it came from one.

source_locator.description: Where within the source this value was read from, recorded so it can be traced back to the text it came from.

mapping_rule_key.description: Which rule in the mapping profile claimed this value, so the interpretation is traceable to the rule that made it.

entity_profile_assignments.description: Records that a configuration profile version applies to one entity in a named role, so that a subject or session can carry configuration its project default does not supply.

entity_id.description: Entity the profile version is assigned to.

profile_version_id.description: Exact profile version being assigned, so the assignment records which content was in force rather than only which profile.

assignment_role.description: The role this profile version plays for the entity. Part of the assignment's identity, so one version can be assigned in more than one role.

assigned_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME created this assignment. An audit time.

recording_profile_assignments.description: Records that a configuration profile version applies to one recording in a named role, and how the recording came to have it. This is where an inherited default becomes an explicit, readable fact about a particular recording.

recording_id.description: Recording the profile version is assigned to.

profile_version_id.description: Exact profile version being assigned, so the assignment records which content was in force.

assignment_role.description: The role this profile version plays for the recording. Part of the assignment's identity, so one version can be assigned in more than one role.

inheritance_source.description: How this recording came to have the assignment: declared directly on it, inherited from a project default, or inherited through an entity it is linked to. Recorded so that an inherited assignment is never mistaken for one the user declared.

assigned_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME created this assignment. An audit time.

recording_epochs.description: A named interval within a recording, such as a phase of a protocol, optionally nested inside another interval of the same recording. Epochs are declared or imported rather than detected by VAWLUME.

epoch_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this interval, generated by the database.

recording_id.description: Recording this interval falls within.

parent_epoch_id.description: Enclosing interval, when this one is nested inside another of the same recording. Null for a top-level interval.

epoch_name.description: Name of the interval as declared. Together with the recording and the interval bounds it forms the epoch's durable identity.

epoch_type.description: What kind of interval this is, when the caller declared a kind. Free text, and null when none was declared.

start_time_s.description: Seconds from the start of the recording at which this interval begins.

end_time_s.description: Seconds from the start of the recording at which this interval ends, never before the start.

source.description: Where the interval came from, defaulting to manual declaration or import. VAWLUME does not detect epochs itself, so this records who said so.

source_file_id.description: Source file this interval was read from, when it was imported from one. Null when it was declared directly.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the interval. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

coordinate_systems.description: A declared spatial frame that positions within a project are expressed in. Two spatial facts are comparable if and only if they cite this same frame by identifier; VAWLUME implements no transformation between frames, so structural similarity between two frames never makes them interchangeable.

coordinate_system_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this frame, generated by the database. Comparability between two spatial facts is decided by comparing this identifier and nothing else.

project_id.description: Project this frame is declared for. Frames are project-scoped shared reference data, cited by anything positioned within the project.

coordinate_system_key.description: Stable identifier for the frame as the project names it, unique within the project.

coordinate_system_name.description: Human-readable name for the frame, used when reporting which space a position was expressed in.

dimensionality.description: Whether the frame is two- or three-dimensional. Two is the working case; three is representable and never required, and a height may only be recorded under a three-dimensional frame.

unit.description: Unit positions in this frame are expressed in, held on the frame so that two comparable facts cannot disagree about it. Free text that VAWLUME never interprets or converts: a pixel frame is legal and supports no real-distance computation, and pixels are never treated as a metric unit.

origin_description.description: Human-readable account of where the frame's origin sits. Provenance for a reader, never applied by any computation.

orientation_description.description: Human-readable account of how the frame's axes are oriented. Provenance for a reader, never applied by any computation.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the frame. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

channel_placements.description: Where one recording channel's microphone was, expressed in one declared frame. The placement attaches to a channel rather than to a device or a setup profile, so it is specific to the session that channel belongs to and cannot claim a position outliving it.

channel_placement_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this placement, generated by the database.

recording_channel_id.description: Channel whose microphone this places, at most one placement per channel. Because a channel belongs to exactly one recording, the placement is session-specific by construction.

coordinate_system_id.description: Frame the coordinates below are expressed in. A placement and the frame it cites must belong to the same project, and a cited frame cannot be deleted while a placement still names it.

position_x.description: Position along the frame's first axis, in the frame's declared unit.

position_y.description: Position along the frame's second axis, in the frame's declared unit.

position_z.description: Height in the frame's declared unit, permitted only under a three-dimensional frame and optional even then. Null means the height is unknown rather than zero.

placement_role.description: What this microphone was for within the arrangement, when the caller declared a role. Free text, and null when none was declared.

orientation_description.description: Human-readable account of which way the microphone faced. Provenance for a reader, never applied by any computation.

source_profile_version_id.description: Device or setup profile version this placement was authored from, when one was cited. Recorded as provenance only: a reusable profile describes many sessions and cannot itself answer where a microphone was during this one.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the placement. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

extractors.description: An external vocalization-detection tool whose output VAWLUME can ingest, registered once and shared across every project in the database. VAWLUME does not run these tools; it interprets what they produced.

extractor_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the tool, generated by the database.

extractor_key.description: Stable identifier for the tool, unique across the database. Composed pair and set keys elsewhere are built by joining these with delimiter sequences, so a key containing one of those sequences is refused by the layer that composes them rather than parsing ambiguously.

extractor_name.description: Human-readable name of the tool as its authors write it. Subject to the same delimiter restriction as the key, because pair labels are composed from names.

description.description: Free-text account of what the tool does and what it emits. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

source_repository.description: Where the tool's own source lives, recorded as a reference for a reader. VAWLUME never fetches or inspects it.

extractor_versions.description: One version of an external extractor. Runs cite a version rather than the tool, because two versions of one detector may disagree about the same audio and pooling their output would erase that difference.

extractor_version_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this version, generated by the database. This is what an extraction run and a declared feature both cite.

extractor_id.description: Tool this is a version of.

version_label.description: Version as reported for the tool. Required when importing any of the three supported extractors and supplied by the caller, because the exports VAWLUME reads carry no trustworthy version of their own.

source_commit_or_tag.description: Source revision the version corresponds to, when the caller knew it. Part of the version's uniqueness, so one label built from two revisions remains two rows.

build_identifier.description: Build or distribution identifier for this version, when one exists. Null when the tool publishes none.

implementation_language.description: Language the tool is implemented in, recorded as context for a reader rather than used by anything.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about this version. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

artifacts.description: A file an extractor produced or consumed, registered as provenance for a run: an export VAWLUME parsed, a settings file, a detector model, or a native container recorded without being read. Registration is a citation, not custody of the contents.

artifact_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the artifact, generated by the database.

project_id.description: Project this artifact was registered under. Its location is unique within the project rather than globally.

source_file_id.description: Registered source file this artifact is, when the same file was also discovered as project source material. Null when the artifact was registered only as extractor provenance.

parent_artifact_id.description: Artifact this one was derived from, such as the native container an export was written out of. Null for an artifact with no recorded antecedent.

artifact_type.description: What role this file plays for VAWLUME, such as the export that was parsed, the settings evidence for a run, or a detector model. This is the reading VAWLUME acts on.

native_artifact_type.description: What the extractor itself calls this kind of file, preserved alongside VAWLUME's reading of it rather than replaced by it.

path_or_uri.description: Location the artifact was registered at, unique within its project.

file_format.description: Format of the file as recorded at registration, normally derived from its extension. Not established by reading the file.

checksum_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file's contents at registration. Relocating the file is recognised as the same file; a change to its contents is a conflict rather than an overwrite. Null when no digest was taken.

is_native.description: Whether this is the extractor's own native container (1) or a derived export (0). A native container is registered as provenance and is generally not parsed.

created_at_source.description: Creation time as the source reported it, in whatever form the source expressed it. Deliberately not recorded as UTC: VAWLUME does not know the zone it was expressed in and will not assert one.

imported_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME registered this artifact. An audit time, and distinct from when the extractor created the file.

metadata_json.description: Extractor-native provenance preserved as JSON text, such as the workspace and dataset names a tool organized its output under. Recorded so the information survives, and deliberately never turned into experimental hierarchy rows.

extraction_runs.description: One execution of one extractor version over declared input recordings. This is the unit that must never be pooled: each run may detect a different number of calls, and detections from separate runs are separate observations of the audio rather than one biological event set.

extraction_run_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the run, generated by the database. Detections, measurements and every downstream analysis cite this to keep one run's output separable from another's.

project_id.description: Project the run belongs to. The run key is unique within the project rather than globally.

extractor_version_id.description: Exact extractor version that produced this run's output. A version rather than a tool, so two versions' output can never be conflated.

run_key.description: Caller-supplied stable identifier for the run, unique within its project and required at import. This is the run's durable identity. Composed set keys elsewhere are built from it, so a key containing one of the sequences those are joined with is refused by the layer that composes them, as it is for extractor keys and names.

run_label.description: Optional human-readable label for the run. Free text with no uniqueness requirement.

output_mapping_profile_version_id.description: Profile version that interpreted this run's export columns. Held separately from the settings profile and never conflated with it: one says how the output was read, the other says how the tool was configured.

settings_profile_version_id.description: Profile version recording how the extractor was configured for this run. Null means the settings were not recoverable, which is recorded as an absence rather than filled with a default the tool may not have used.

started_at_utc.description: UTC time the extractor run began, when the caller knew it. Null when the export carries no such evidence.

completed_at_utc.description: UTC time the extractor run finished, when the caller knew it. Null when the export carries no such evidence.

imported_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME imported this run. An audit time about the import, not about the extraction.

status.description: State of the run, drawn from a declared vocabulary that separates one merely planned, one still running, one the extractor completed, one VAWLUME has imported, and one that failed. Import is the ordinary state for a run whose output was read from an existing export.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the run, including provenance the schema has no column for, such as the source row order of an export. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

extraction_run_inputs.description: Records that a recording, optionally one channel of it, was an input to an extraction run. A detection may only name a recording registered here; a trigger refuses one that is not, so a run cannot acquire detections from audio it never declared reading.

recording_id.description: Recording the run consumed.

recording_channel_id.description: Particular channel consumed, when the run read one channel rather than the recording as a whole. Null for a whole-recording input.

input_role.description: How the run used this input, defaulting to source audio. Part of the input's identity, so one recording can be supplied to a run in more than one role.

extraction_run_profiles.description: Records that a configuration profile version applies to an extraction run in a named role, and how the run came to have it. This is where a profile inherited from a recording or a project default becomes an explicit fact about a particular run.

extraction_run_id.description: Run the profile version is assigned to.

profile_version_id.description: Exact profile version being assigned, so the assignment records which content was in force.

assignment_role.description: The role this profile version plays for the run. Part of the assignment's identity, so one version can be assigned in more than one role.

inheritance_source.description: How this run came to have the assignment: declared directly on it, or inherited from the recording, a project default, or an entity. Recorded so that an inherited assignment is never mistaken for one the user declared.

extraction_run_artifacts.description: Records that a registered artifact belongs to an extraction run in a named role, which is how a run cites the export it was read from alongside the settings and model evidence supporting it.

artifact_role.description: What this artifact is to the run, such as the parsed export or supporting evidence. Part of the citation's identity, so one artifact can serve a run in more than one role.

extractor_objects.description: One node of the container hierarchy an extractor emitted in its own terms, such as its notion of an audio file, a processing pass, or a syllable set, preserved alongside VAWLUME's reading of what that node corresponds to. Rows exist only where an extractor's profile declares an emitted hierarchy; an export that declares none produces no rows here.

extractor_object_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this node, generated by the database.

extraction_run_id.description: Run whose output this node came from. The hierarchy is per run, because it is the extractor's own organization of that run's output.

parent_object_id.description: Enclosing node, when this one is nested inside another from the same run. Null for a top-level node, which is what makes the nesting readable without a separate depth column.

source_artifact_id.description: Artifact this node was read from. Null when the node was inferred from the run rather than from a particular file.

native_level.description: The extractor's own word for this level of its hierarchy, preserved as the tool expressed it rather than translated.

canonical_level.description: VAWLUME's reading of what the native level corresponds to, such as a recording, an extraction run, or an event. The added canonical interpretation; the native level remains the tool's own.

canonical_subtype.description: Finer canonical reading within the level, where the level alone does not say enough about what the node holds. Null when no subtype was assigned.

equivalence_class.description: Label grouping nodes that different extractors express differently but that mean the same thing, so that two tools' hierarchies can be compared without either being rewritten into the other's vocabulary.

native_id.description: The extractor's own identifier for this node, preserved as expressed. Unique within its run, level and parent, which is scoping rather than a claim of durable cross-artifact identity.

native_label.description: The extractor's own human-readable name for this node, when it provided one.

mapping_strength.description: How firmly the native level was read as the canonical one, recorded because that reading is an interpretation and its confidence varies between tools rather than being uniform.

lineage_note.description: Free-text account of where this node came from and how it was interpreted. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

extractor_object_recordings.description: Records which recordings one extractor-native node covers. A separate table because an extractor container may span several recordings, so the relationship cannot be a single column on the node.

extractor_object_id.description: Extractor-native node being mapped to a recording.

recording_id.description: Recording the node covers.

membership_role.description: How the recording relates to the node, defaulting to plain membership. Part of the mapping's identity, so one recording can relate to a node in more than one way.

canonical_features.description: VAWLUME's own vocabulary of measurable quantities, defined once so a native measurement can be given an interpretable reading in shared terms. Sharing a canonical feature is not what makes two extractors' measurements comparable: that judgement is registered separately, pair by pair, and two tools computing a quantity by different methods are deliberately given different canonical names rather than merged under one.

canonical_feature_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the canonical feature, generated by the database.

canonical_name.description: VAWLUME's name for the quantity, unique across the database. Names a definition rather than asserting comparability: two extractors measuring nominally the same thing by different methods carry different canonical names on purpose, because merging them would assert that the two statistics are one.

feature_domain.description: Broad area the quantity belongs to, such as timing or spectral content, used to group the vocabulary for a reader.

value_type.description: Kind of value this feature takes, which determines which typed column a measurement of it populates.

canonical_unit.description: Unit VAWLUME expresses this feature in, which is what a native unit is converted to when a mapping declares a transform. Null for a feature carrying no unit.

definition.description: What the quantity means, written so that two extractors' measurements can be judged against one definition rather than against each other.

is_vawlume_derived.description: Whether VAWLUME defines this feature itself (1) rather than adopting it from what extractors already emit (0). A derived feature is VAWLUME's own product and should not be read as an extractor observation.

extractor_features.description: One quantity that a particular extractor version declares it emits, described in the extractor's own terms. Registration is what makes a measurement interpretable; a column an extractor writes but no version declares here has no registered meaning.

extractor_feature_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this declared feature, generated by the database. Every measurement cites it, which is how a stored number keeps the identity of what produced it.

extractor_version_id.description: Extractor version that declares this feature. Declared per version because what a tool emits, and what it means by it, can change between versions.

native_name.description: The extractor's own name for the quantity, preserved exactly as the tool writes it.

native_unit.description: Unit the extractor expresses this quantity in, as the extractor expresses it. Preserved rather than converted; conversion, where it happens at all, is recorded on the measurement.

value_type.description: Kind of value this feature takes, which determines which typed column a native measurement of it populates.

native_definition.description: What the extractor says the quantity means, in the extractor's own terms. The basis on which any claim of comparability with another tool's feature has to be judged.

source_artifact_type.description: Which kind of artifact this feature appears in, since one extractor may emit different quantities in different outputs.

derivation_stage.description: How far through the extractor's own processing this quantity is produced, which matters because a raw and a post-processed version of nominally the same quantity are not the same measurement.

measurement_method.description: How the extractor arrives at the value, recorded because two tools reporting the same nominal quantity by different methods may not be comparable.

operational_variant.description: Which variant of a quantity this is, where one extractor emits more than one operational definition of nominally the same thing. A measurement join must select the intended variant rather than assume a canonical feature has exactly one native counterpart.

equivalence_class.description: Label grouping features that different extractors express differently but that refer to the same underlying quantity, used as a starting point for comparability rather than as a claim of it.

source_reference.description: Where in the extractor's own documentation this feature is described, recorded so a reader can check the native definition against its source.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about this declared feature. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

feature_mappings.description: Declares how one extractor's feature relates to one of VAWLUME's canonical features, under a particular mapping profile version. This is a recorded judgement about correspondence, including the judgement that two things do not correspond.

feature_mapping_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this mapping, generated by the database.

canonical_feature_id.description: Canonical feature it is mapped to.

mapping_profile_version_id.description: Profile version that declared this mapping, so a correspondence judgement is attributable to the document that made it. Part of the mapping's uniqueness, so two profile versions may declare different mappings for one pair. Null for a mapping seeded with the repository rather than authored.

mapping_type.description: How strong the correspondence is, drawn from a declared vocabulary running from convertible by a stated transform, through conceptually equivalent, comparable, and merely related, to explicitly not comparable. Recording that two features are not comparable is a result, not an omission.

transform_key.description: Named transform converting the native value to the canonical one, from a fixed whitelist rather than an arbitrary function name. Null when no conversion applies.

preserve_raw.description: Whether the native value is retained alongside any converted one. Defaults to true, because canonicalization is meant to add an interpretable reading rather than replace what the extractor said.

notes.description: Free-text justification or caveat for this mapping. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

feature_relationships.description: Declares how one extractor's feature relates to another extractor's feature directly, rather than through the canonical vocabulary. This registry is what decides whether a cross-extractor comparison of a quantity is admissible at all.

feature_relationship_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this pairing, generated by the database.

feature_a_id.description: One endpoint of the pairing. The a and b endpoints are ordered by identifier rather than by role, which is a constraint that keeps one conceptual pairing from being stored twice in opposite directions; neither side is privileged and any asymmetry of role is recorded separately.

feature_b_id.description: The other endpoint of the pairing, always the higher identifier of the two. As with the a endpoint, the position carries ordering rather than meaning.

relationship_type.description: How strong the correspondence is, drawn from the same declared vocabulary the canonical mappings use, running from convertible by a stated transform to explicitly not comparable.

comparison_method.description: How the two features may legitimately be compared, when the relationship type alone does not say. Recorded because two tools measuring nominally the same quantity by different methods may need a stated basis for comparison.

unit_normalization.description: What must be done to the two sides' units before their values can be compared. Null when the sides already agree.

consilience_eligible.description: Whether the registry considers this pairing defensible enough to compare. Necessary but not sufficient: a comparison also requires the two sides' canonical units to agree. An ineligible pairing is still reported as one that exists, and is excluded from every comparison and summary, so exclusion is visible rather than silent.

default_role.description: Which side is treated as the reference when a comparison needs one. This is where an asymmetry of role is recorded, since the endpoint ordering itself carries none.

justification.description: Why this correspondence is claimed, written so that the claim can be assessed rather than taken. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

source_reference.description: Where the evidence for this correspondence comes from, recorded so a reader can check it against its source.

detections.description: One event an extractor reported in one recording during one run, with its timing as the extractor gave it. A detection is an observation by a particular tool, not an established vocalization: two runs over the same audio may report different numbers of them and neither is the truth the other failed to find.

detection_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the detection, generated by the database.

extraction_run_id.description: Run that reported this detection. Detections are only ever compared across runs through the matching layer, never pooled by being read together.

recording_id.description: Recording the event was reported in. Must already be registered as an input to the run, which a trigger enforces.

source_artifact_id.description: Artifact this detection was read from. Part of the detection's uniqueness within its run, so one run reading two exports keeps their events distinct.

extractor_object_id.description: Node of the extractor's own hierarchy this detection sits under, when the extractor emitted one. Null for an export that declares no container hierarchy.

native_event_id.description: The extractor's own identifier for the event, preserved as expressed. Often an ordinal within one export rather than a durable identifier: the same values may legally recur in another run or another tool's output, so it identifies the event only within its run, recording and artifact.

event_subtype.description: What kind of event this row records, defaulting to a vocalization detection. Present so the table can hold event kinds other than calls without a parallel table.

start_time_s.description: Onset in seconds from the start of the recording, as the extractor reported it. Never rewritten by alignment; a time expressed on another clock is derived on demand from stored coefficients instead.

end_time_s.description: Offset in seconds from the start of the recording, never before the onset, as the extractor reported it.

timing_basis.description: Which of the extractor's own quantities the stored onset and offset were taken from, recorded because an export may carry several timing columns and the one chosen is a mapping decision rather than an obvious fact.

detection_score.description: The extractor's own confidence or model score for this event, on the extractor's own scale and uncalibrated. Null when the extractor emits no score at all, which is the case for two of the three supported tools; absence here is a property of the producer rather than a failed import.

imported_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME imported this detection. An audit time about the import, not about the event.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the detection, including provenance with no column of its own such as the source row position it was read from. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

event_measurements.description: One measured quantity for one detection, holding the extractor's value and VAWLUME's canonicalized reading of it side by side. Both are kept because canonicalization adds an interpretable representation and is never allowed to erase what the extractor actually said.

event_measurement_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this measurement, generated by the database.

extractor_feature_id.description: Extractor-declared feature this is a measurement of, which is what makes the stored number interpretable. Required, because a value whose declared meaning is unknown is not a measurement.

canonical_feature_id.description: Canonical feature the measurement was read as, when a mapping declared one. Null when the quantity has no canonical counterpart, which leaves the native value intact and simply uninterpreted in VAWLUME's own vocabulary.

source_artifact_id.description: Artifact this value was read from.

native_value_type.description: Which of the native typed columns carries the extractor's value, or the declared absence of one. A constraint enforces that exactly one is populated, and that none is when the value is absent, so a measurement the extractor could not make is never confused with a zero.

native_raw_token.description: The original lexical token as it appeared in the export, before any parsing. Text even when it looks numeric, because it records what the source wrote rather than a number VAWLUME computed, and a sentinel or blank is preserved here as the explicit missingness it represents.

native_value_real.description: The extractor's value when it is a real number, and null otherwise.

native_value_integer.description: The extractor's value when it is an integer, and null otherwise.

native_value_text.description: The extractor's value when it is textual, and null otherwise.

native_value_boolean.description: The extractor's value when it is a truth value, stored as 0 or 1, and null otherwise.

native_value_json.description: The extractor's value when it is a structured payload, stored as JSON text, and null otherwise.

native_unit.description: Unit the extractor expressed this value in, as the extractor expressed it.

canonical_value_real.description: The canonicalized reading when it is a real number, and null otherwise. Present alongside the native value rather than instead of it.

canonical_value_integer.description: The canonicalized reading when it is an integer, and null otherwise.

canonical_value_text.description: The canonicalized reading when it is textual, and null otherwise.

canonical_value_boolean.description: The canonicalized reading when it is a truth value, stored as 0 or 1, and null otherwise.

canonical_value_json.description: The canonicalized reading when it is a structured payload, stored as JSON text, and null otherwise.

canonical_unit.description: Unit the canonicalized reading is expressed in, which may differ from the native unit when a transform was applied.

transform_key.description: Named transform that produced the canonical value from the native one, from a fixed whitelist. Null when no conversion was applied, including when the value was absent and therefore had nothing to convert.

operational_variant.description: Which variant of the quantity this measurement is, carried on the row so that a join selecting one canonical feature can still tell two operational definitions apart.

source_locator.description: Where in the source artifact this value was read from, recorded so a stored number can be traced back to the cell it came from.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about this measurement. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

unmapped_source_values.description: A value present in an extractor's output that no mapping profile claimed, preserved row by row with where it came from. Retaining it is the point: an unrecognized column is evidence whose meaning is not yet mapped, not noise to be discarded.

unmapped_value_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this preserved value, generated by the database.

extraction_run_id.description: Run whose output the value appeared in. Null when the value is scoped more narrowly and the run is reachable through that scope instead.

detection_id.description: Detection the value belonged to, when it appeared on an event row. Null for a value that was not per-event.

extractor_object_id.description: Node of the extractor's hierarchy the value belonged to, when it appeared at container level rather than on an event.

source_artifact_id.description: Artifact the value was read from.

native_field_name.description: The column or field name as the extractor wrote it, preserved exactly, since that name is most of what a later reader has to work out what the value meant.

raw_value_text.description: The value exactly as it appeared, held as text because it was never parsed into a typed value. Nothing was inferred about what kind of quantity it is.

native_unit.description: Unit the source stated for this value, when it stated one. Recorded without being interpreted.

source_locator.description: Where in the source artifact the value was read from, so it can be traced back to the cell it came from.

reason_unmapped.description: Why no mapping claimed the value, such as a column the profile does not declare. Distinguishes a value nobody described from a value deliberately excluded.

mapping_profile_version_id.description: Profile version that was in force when the value went unclaimed, so a later revision of the profile can be checked against what it previously failed to describe.

curation_events.description: A recorded act of review or state change on one detection, attributed to whoever performed it. Review state is evidence about a detection, never a filter applied to it: a detection marked rejected is still imported and still present.

curation_event_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this review record, generated by the database.

source_artifact_id.description: Artifact the review state was read from.

action_type.description: What was done to the detection, such as accepting or rejecting it, preserving the source's own term for the act.

status_after.description: State the detection was in once the act was recorded. Held separately from the act because the same act may leave different states in different tools' vocabularies.

actor_type.description: Who performed the act, distinguishing the extractor's own automatic state from a human reviewer, from VAWLUME itself, and from an unknown actor. An extractor's own review flag never becomes a human reviewer: no reviewer is invented from an export that states only a state.

actor_label.description: Identifier or name for the actor, when the source named one. Null when the source recorded only a state and not who set it.

event_time_utc.description: UTC time the review act occurred, when the source recorded one. Null when the export carries no such evidence.

details_json.description: Further structured detail about the act, preserved as JSON text where the schema has no dedicated column for it.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the review act. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

classification_runs.description: One labelling of an extraction run's detections, whether by a model, by clustering, or by hand. Kept separate from detection so that label evidence can be recorded without asserting that a label is a biological fact about the call.

classification_run_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this labelling, generated by the database.

parent_extraction_run_id.description: Extraction run whose detections are being labelled. A label assignment may only concern a detection from this run, which a trigger enforces.

extractor_object_id.description: Node of the extractor's hierarchy the labelling was scoped to, when it was scoped more narrowly than the whole run.

model_artifact_id.description: Registered model that produced the labels, when one was supplied. Null when the source states labels without saying what produced them, and a model is never inferred from the extractor's version or its defaults.

settings_profile_version_id.description: Profile version recording how the labelling was configured, when that was recoverable.

method.description: How the labels were arrived at. An export that states labels without saying whether they were manual, supervised, or clustering-derived is recorded as exactly that unstated provenance rather than assigned a plausible method.

run_label.description: Optional human-readable label for this labelling. Free text.

number_of_classes.description: How many classes the labelling distinguishes, when that was stated. Null when the source did not say.

created_at_utc.description: UTC time the labelling was produced, when the source recorded one.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the labelling. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

classification_classes.description: One class a labelling can assign, holding the source's own term for it and, separately, any canonical reading of that term. The native token is preserved exactly and acquires no biological meaning by being stored.

classification_class_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this class, generated by the database.

classification_run_id.description: Labelling this class belongs to. Classes are per labelling, because the same word may mean different things in two labellings.

native_class_id.description: The source's own identifier for the class, unique within its labelling.

native_class_label.description: The source's own name for the class, preserved exactly as written.

canonical_class_label.description: VAWLUME's reading of what the class corresponds to, when a caller declared one. Null when the source's label has been preserved without any canonical meaning being claimed for it, which is the ordinary case for an imported label of unstated provenance.

description.description: Free-text account of what the class is taken to mean. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

classification_assignments.description: Records that one labelling assigned one class to one detection, with the score behind it where the source gave one. At most one assignment per detection per labelling, so a labelling states one answer rather than several.

classification_assignment_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this assignment, generated by the database.

detection_id.description: Detection being labelled. Must belong to the labelling's parent extraction run, which a trigger enforces.

classification_class_id.description: Class assigned. Must be one of the classes belonging to this same labelling, which a trigger enforces.

score_or_distance.description: The number behind the assignment, which may be a confidence or a distance depending on the method. On the source's own scale and uncalibrated; its direction of goodness is a property of the method rather than of this column.

assignment_source.description: Who or what made the assignment, defaulting to the extractor. Distinguishes a label imported from an export from one added afterwards.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the assignment. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

analysis_runs.description: One execution of a VAWLUME analysis over material already in the database, such as matching two extraction runs or composing agreement across several. Analyses are immutable: a changed specification or algorithm produces a new run rather than altering what an existing one concluded.

analysis_run_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the run, generated by the database. Everything an analysis derives cites this, which is what keeps one analysis's conclusions separable from another's over the same detections.

project_id.description: Project the analysis belongs to. Its run key is unique within the project rather than globally.

parent_analysis_run_id.description: Analysis this one is a child of, for a derivation with a single genuine parent such as the agreement-statistics run hanging off a matching analysis. Null for a run with no single parent, including one composed from several sources, whose lineage is recorded in its own relation rather than forced into this column.

run_type.description: What kind of analysis this is, such as pairwise matching, cross-extractor agreement statistics, or arbitrary-N agreement composition. An open vocabulary rather than a constrained one, though some values carry enforced consequences: agreement groups may only hang off a run declaring the arbitrary-N agreement type.

run_key.description: Caller-supplied stable identifier for the analysis, unique within its project. Where a change of algorithm or specification would change what the run means, the convention is to build that version into the key, so a rerun under new assumptions becomes a new run rather than silently redefining an old one.

run_label.description: Optional human-readable label for the analysis. Free text with no uniqueness requirement.

vawlume_version.description: Version of VAWLUME the caller asserted was in use. Supplied on the run specification and never inferred from the working tree, so it records a claim rather than a verified fact.

source_commit.description: Source revision the caller asserted was in use. Like the version, a caller claim VAWLUME records without checking.

status.description: State of the analysis, drawn from a declared vocabulary that separates one still in progress from one that completed, one that completed with warnings, and one that failed. Derived rows are written inside the transaction that completes a run, so a completed run's graph is whole.

started_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when the analysis began.

completed_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when the analysis finished. Null while it is unfinished or if it never reached a terminal state.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the analysis. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

analysis_run_profiles.description: Records that a configuration profile version governed an analysis in a named role, which is how a stored conclusion stays attributable to the specification that produced it.

profile_version_id.description: Exact profile version in force, including its checksum-bearing content. A conclusion is only reproducible if the rules behind it can be recovered exactly.

assignment_role.description: The role this profile version played for the analysis, such as the matching specification or the agreement specification. Part of the assignment's identity, so one version can govern a run in more than one role.

analysis_run_extraction_inputs.description: Declares which extraction runs an analysis was permitted to draw detections from. This is the boundary that makes an analysis's population explicit: a group may only contain detections from a run declared here, and a trigger enforces it.

extraction_run_id.description: Extraction run whose detections the analysis may consider.

input_role.description: How the analysis used this input. Part of the declaration's identity, so one extraction run can be supplied to an analysis in more than one role.

analysis_run_sources.description: Records that one analysis was composed from another. An analysis over three extractors consumes three pairwise analyses and has no single parent among them, so multi-source lineage lives here rather than being forced into a single parent column.

analysis_run_id.description: Derived analysis, the one that consumed the other.

source_analysis_run_id.description: Analysis that was consumed, which may not be the derived analysis itself. A cited source cannot be deleted while the derived analysis still stands, because a stored conclusion must not outlive the evidence it was composed from.

dependency_role.description: How the source contributed to the derived analysis. Descriptive rather than part of identity: one source contributes to one derived analysis once, so the pair alone identifies the dependency.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about this dependency. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

candidate_pairs.description: One pair of detections from different extraction runs that an analysis considered as possibly the same event, together with the temporal measures that informed the decision. A candidate is evidence that two detections were compared, not a claim that they correspond; the conclusion is recorded separately.

candidate_pair_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the candidate, generated by the database.

analysis_run_id.description: Analysis that considered this pair. The pair is unique within its analysis, so two analyses may reach different conclusions about the same two detections.

recording_id.description: Recording both detections belong to. A trigger refuses a pair whose detections do not both come from this recording.

detection_a_id.description: One endpoint of the pair, always the lower of the two identifiers. The ordering is by identifier rather than by run or role, and exists so one conceptual pair cannot be stored twice in opposite directions; neither endpoint is privileged and neither denotes a particular extractor.

detection_b_id.description: The other endpoint, always the higher identifier. As with the a endpoint, the position carries ordering rather than meaning, and a consumer that needs to know which extractor a side came from resolves it through the detection rather than from this column.

temporal_overlap_s.description: Seconds the two detections overlap in the recording's own timebase. Zero-length overlap is not a candidate: the analysis considers a pair only where overlap is positive.

temporal_iou.description: Intersection over union of the two intervals, between zero and one. The measure the candidate threshold is applied to, and uncalibrated: the floor it is compared against is declared in the specification and is illustrative rather than validated.

onset_difference_s.description: Difference between the two detections' onsets, in seconds. Stored alongside the other measures rather than combined into a single score, because the layer reports several transparent measures instead of one number.

offset_difference_s.description: Difference between the two detections' offsets, in seconds.

duration_difference_s.description: Difference between the two detections' durations, in seconds.

candidate_score.description: The specification's own score for the candidate, whose definition travels with that specification rather than being fixed by this column. Uncalibrated, and deliberately not a blend of the separate measures above: the layer reports several transparent measures rather than combining them into one number that would read like a probability.

candidate_status.description: What the analysis concluded about the pair, defaulting to its being a candidate. Records the pair's standing within the analysis rather than a judgement about the underlying events.

details_json.description: Further structured detail about how the pair was evaluated, preserved as JSON text where the schema has no dedicated column for it.

match_groups.description: A connected component of detections that one pairwise analysis grouped together for one recording, with the topology that membership implies. Groups come from graph connectivity over candidate edges: there is no optimizer, no score winner, and no forced one-to-one assignment.

match_group_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the group, generated by the database. A storage identity: the group's scientific identity for rerun comparison is its ordered membership, not this number.

analysis_run_id.description: Analysis that formed this group. Every detection in the analysis's inputs belongs to exactly one of its groups, which a trigger enforces.

recording_id.description: Recording the grouped detections belong to. Grouping is per recording.

match_type.description: Topology of the group, from a declared vocabulary covering one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one, many-to-many, an explicitly unmatched single member, and an ambiguous case. Derived from member counts on the ordered run pair alone. Split and merge readings of the uneven topologies are relative descriptions of what two runs did, never claims about what happened biologically.

ambiguity_status.description: Whether the topology leaves the correspondence unambiguous, ambiguous, or unmatched. Held separately from the topology because it is the consequence a consumer usually needs, and because ambiguity outranks feature evidence in every downstream judgement.

match_score.description: Score for the group as a whole. Left null by the current matching implementation, which specifies no component score; a number here would have to be defined before it could be read as anything.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the group, carrying the stable membership key and member counts that constitute the group's rerun identity. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

match_group_members.description: Records that one detection belongs to one match group. Membership is a partition within an analysis: a detection appears in exactly one group of a given analysis, and in as many analyses as have considered it.

detection_id.description: Detection that belongs to it. Must come from one of the analysis's declared extraction inputs and must not already belong to another group of the same analysis; triggers enforce both.

member_role.description: Which side of the ordered run pair this detection came from, where the group's topology needs the sides distinguished.

consensus_events.description: An interval derived from a match group's members under a declared boundary rule: VAWLUME's own reading of when the event occurred, given that several extractors reported it. Derived rather than observed, and emitted only for topologies the specification permits — a many-to-many or unmatched group yields none.

consensus_event_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the derived event, generated by the database.

match_group_id.description: Group the event was derived from, whose membership it repeats exactly. Null when the group it came from is no longer present, which leaves the derived interval without its lineage rather than removing it.

recording_id.description: Recording the derived interval falls in.

start_time_s.description: Derived onset in seconds from the recording's start, computed from member detections under the declared boundary rule. A VAWLUME product, not an extractor observation, and it never overwrites any member's native timing.

end_time_s.description: Derived offset in seconds, never before the derived onset, computed under the same boundary rule.

derivation_method.description: Which boundary rule produced the interval, such as the mean of the members' boundaries or their union. Recorded because the two answer different questions: a mean speaks for an unambiguous correspondence, a union preserves the extent of an ambiguous one.

consensus_status.description: Whether the derivation was over an unambiguous correspondence or one whose ambiguity the boundary rule preserved. Distinguishes an interval two extractors agreed on from one that spans a split or merge without resolving it.

confidence_score.description: Confidence in the derived event. Left null by the current implementation, which defines no calibrated confidence model; a number here would need one before it could be interpreted.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the derived event. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

consensus_event_members.description: Records which detections a consensus event was derived from, repeating its match group's membership exactly. Kept as its own relation so a derived interval carries its evidence rather than pointing at a group a reader must then resolve.

consensus_event_id.description: Derived event the detection contributed to.

member_role.description: Which side of the ordered run pair this detection came from, carried over from the match group.

consilience_assessments.description: One automated categorical judgement about a match group or a consensus event, assigned by a frozen rule set carried in a versioned specification. A summary of what evidence was available under one set of assumptions, never a verdict on whether a vocalization occurred.
