offset_difference_s.description: Signed difference in seconds between the compared window and target offsets under the declared comparison basis. Its sign follows the correspondence method rather than an inferred universal convention.

iou_basis.description: Declares whether temporal overlap and IoU were evaluated on native intervals or after alignment. This distinction is necessary because a piecewise clock transform can change interval duration.

start_extrapolated.description: Boolean flag recording whether the aligned start lay outside the transform's anchored span when that condition was assessed. Null means no extrapolation flag was recorded, not that extrapolation is impossible.

end_extrapolated.description: Boolean flag recording whether the aligned end lay outside the transform's anchored span when that condition was assessed. It preserves alignment reliability evidence rather than resolving the match.

eligibility_rule.description: Declared attribution-specific rule that determined whether this window-target pair was eligible for correspondence. It is distinct from detector-to-detector matching specifications.

min_temporal_iou.description: Minimum temporal-IoU threshold applied by the eligibility rule when one was recorded. It is a method parameter, not a calibrated probability or a claim that this was the only acceptance criterion.

notes.description: Additional context about this measured window-to-target correspondence, including ambiguity or method detail not represented elsewhere. Never parsed as a selected match or caller decision.

v_sequence_members.description: Sequence membership joined to its owning sequence, so an ordered event list can be read together with the analysis run, recording, epoch, and scope that define it without writing the join by hand.

relationships.description: Each configuration profile that names a project belongs to that project. A profile with no project is built in and applies to every project in the database.
Each registered version is a version of exactly one configuration profile. A profile accumulates versions over time and none of them replaces another.
Each project-level assignment names the exact profile version it assigns. The cited version cannot be deleted while the assignment stands.
Each project-level assignment names the project it applies to, and is removed with that project.
Each registered source file was discovered within one project, and its location is unique within that project rather than globally.
Each ingestion attempt names the exact mapping profile version that interpreted its sources, which is what makes the rows it produced traceable to the rules that produced them.
Each ingestion attempt is an attempt to ingest one project.
Each per-file outcome names the source file it reports on.
Each per-file outcome belongs to the ingestion attempt that produced it, so one file can have a different outcome in each attempt.
Each hierarchy level belongs to one project, because two projects may use the same native word for different levels.
Each entity records the ingestion attempt that first created it. Later compatible attempts leave this provenance alone and record their own audit rows instead.
Each entity sits at exactly one level of its project's hierarchy, and its native identifier is unique only within that level.
Each entity belongs to one project.
Each relationship may cite the source file it was read from, when it came from a single file.
Each relationship records the ingestion attempt that first created it, when it arose from one.
Names the contained or subordinate endpoint of the relationship. This is the child side; the parent side is a separate reference into the same table, and the two may not name the same entity.

Names the containing or superior endpoint of the relationship. This is the parent side, distinct from the child reference into the same table, and which endpoint is which is part of the relationship's meaning.
Each relationship belongs to the project both of its endpoints belong to.
Each attribute may cite the source file its value was read from.
Each attribute records the ingestion attempt that first created it, when it arose from one.
Each attribute describes exactly one entity and is removed with it.

Each recording is anchored to exactly one registered source file, and each such file backs at most one recording. This one-to-one anchor is the recording's durable identity and the boundary extractor imports resolve against.
Each recording belongs to one project.
Each channel belongs to exactly one recording, which is what makes anything attached to a channel specific to that session.
Each participation record names the ingestion attempt that first created it, when it arose from one.
Names the entity that took part in the recording.
Names the recording the entity took part in. One entity may be linked to one recording more than once under different roles or intervals.
Each attribute may cite the source file its value was read from.
Each attribute records the ingestion attempt that first created it, when it arose from one.
Each attribute describes exactly one recording and is removed with it.
Each entity-level assignment names the exact profile version it assigns. The cited version cannot be deleted while the assignment stands.
Each entity-level assignment names the entity it applies to, and is removed with that entity.
Each recording-level assignment names the exact profile version it assigns. The cited version cannot be deleted while the assignment stands.
Each recording-level assignment names the recording it applies to, whether the recording was given it directly or inherited it.
Each interval may cite the source file it was imported from, and cites none when it was declared directly.

Names the enclosing interval when this one is nested inside another of the same recording. A top-level interval names none, so the column is what distinguishes nesting depth rather than a separate level column.
Each interval falls within exactly one recording, and its bounds are seconds from that recording's start.
Each declared frame belongs to one project and is shared reference data within it.

Each placement may cite the device or setup profile version it was authored from. Provenance only: a reusable profile describes many sessions and does not itself assert where a microphone was during this one.

Each placement expresses its coordinates in exactly one declared frame, which must belong to the same project as the channel. A frame cannot be deleted while a placement still cites it, because coordinates in no declared space would be worse than refusing the delete.
Each placement positions exactly one channel's microphone, and a channel has at most one placement. A microphone moved mid-session is therefore unrepresentable rather than silently averaged.
Each registered version is a version of exactly one extractor tool.
Names the artifact this one was derived from, such as the native container an export was written out of. An artifact with no recorded antecedent names none.
Each artifact may cite the registered source file it is, when the same file was also discovered as project source material. An artifact registered only as extractor provenance cites none.
Each artifact is registered under one project, and its location is unique within that project rather than globally.
Names the profile version recording how the extractor was configured for this run. A run names none when its settings were not recoverable, which is an absence rather than a default.

Names the profile version that interpreted this run's export columns. A separate reference from the settings one, because how the output was read and how the tool was configured are different facts and are never conflated.
Each run was produced by exactly one extractor version, and that version cannot be deleted while the run cites it.
Each run belongs to one project, within which its run key is unique.
Names the particular channel consumed, when the run read one channel rather than the whole recording. A whole-recording input names none.
Names the recording the run consumed. This declaration is what makes a detection on that recording admissible for the run.
Names the run that consumed this input.
Each run-level assignment names the exact profile version it assigns. The cited version cannot be deleted while the assignment stands.
Each run-level assignment names the run it applies to, whether the run was given it directly or inherited it.
Names the artifact the run cites in this role.
Names the run the artifact belongs to.
Names the artifact this hierarchy node was read from. A node inferred from the run rather than from a particular file names none.

Names the enclosing node when this one is nested inside another from the same run. A top-level node names none, which is what makes the extractor's own nesting readable without a separate depth column.
Each hierarchy node belongs to one run, because it is that run's own organization of its output rather than a shared structure.
Names a recording the extractor-native node covers.
Names the extractor-native node being mapped. A node may cover several recordings, which is why this mapping is a table rather than a column.
Each declared feature belongs to one extractor version, because what a tool emits and what it means by it can change between versions.
Names the profile version that declared this correspondence, so the judgement is attributable to the document that made it. A mapping seeded with the repository rather than authored names none.
Names the canonical feature the extractor's feature is mapped to.
Names the extractor-declared feature being mapped.

Names the higher-identifier endpoint of the pairing. The two endpoint references into this one table are ordered by identifier so that a pairing cannot be stored twice in opposite directions; the position carries ordering rather than role.

Names the lower-identifier endpoint of the pairing, and is the other of the two references into this one table. Which side is a reference for a comparison is recorded on the pairing itself, not by this position.
Names the node of the extractor's own hierarchy this detection sits under. A detection from an export declaring no container hierarchy names none.
Names the artifact this detection was read from, and forms part of the detection's uniqueness within its run so that one run reading two exports keeps their events distinct.
Names the recording the event was reported in. That recording must already be a declared input to the detection's run, which a trigger enforces.
Names the run that reported this detection. Reading two runs' detections together is a matching operation and never a simple union of these rows.
Names the artifact this value was read from.
Names the canonical feature this value was read as. A measurement of a quantity with no canonical counterpart names none, and remains a preserved native value rather than becoming an error.
Names the extractor-declared feature this is a measurement of, which is what makes the stored number interpretable. Required, and the feature cannot be deleted while measurements cite it.
Names the detection this measurement describes. One detection carries many measurements, and may carry more than one of nominally the same quantity under different operational variants.
Names the profile version in force when this value went unclaimed, so a later revision can be checked against what it previously failed to describe.
Names the artifact the unclaimed value was read from.
Scopes the unclaimed value to a node of the extractor's hierarchy, when it appeared at container level. One of several alternative scopes, and null when the value belongs to a different one.
Scopes the unclaimed value to one detection, when it appeared on an event row. The narrowest of the alternative scopes, and the usual one for an unrecognized column in a per-event export.
Scopes the unclaimed value to a run, when it belongs to the output as a whole rather than to any one event or container.
Names the artifact the review state was read from.
Names the detection the review act concerns. A detection may accumulate several review acts, and none of them removes it.
Names the profile version recording how the labelling was configured, when that was recoverable.

Names the registered model that produced the labels, when one was supplied. A labelling whose source states labels without saying what produced them names none, and no model is inferred to fill the gap.
Scopes the labelling to a node of the extractor's hierarchy, when it covered less than the whole run.
Names the extraction run whose detections are being labelled. An assignment may only concern a detection from this run, which a trigger enforces.
Each labelling belongs to one project.
Each class belongs to one labelling, because the same word may mean different things in two labellings and a shared class table would assert otherwise.
Names the class assigned, which must be one of the classes belonging to this same labelling; a trigger enforces that.
Names the labelling that made this assignment. One detection may be assigned a class by several labellings, but at most once by each.
Names the detection being labelled, which must belong to the labelling's parent extraction run; a trigger enforces that.

Names the analysis this one is a child of, for a derivation with a single genuine parent. A run composed from several sources names none here and records its lineage in the sources relation instead, so this column is never overloaded to mean one of several.
Each analysis belongs to one project, within which its run key is unique.

Names the exact profile version that governed the analysis in this role. The cited version cannot be deleted while the analysis stands, because a conclusion whose rules had vanished would be unreproducible.
Names the analysis the profile version governed.
Names an extraction run the analysis was permitted to draw detections from. This declaration is what bounds the analysis's population, and a group member from an undeclared run is refused.
Names the analysis consuming this extraction run.
Names the analysis that was consumed. One of two references into this same table, and the one that cannot be deleted while the derived analysis stands.
Names the derived analysis that did the consuming. The other of the two references into this table, and never the same analysis as the source; both must belong to one project.

Names the higher-identifier endpoint of the considered pair. The two endpoint references into this one table are ordered by identifier so a pair cannot be stored twice in opposite directions; the position carries ordering rather than extractor or role.

Names the lower-identifier endpoint, and is the other of the two references into this table. The two detections must come from distinct extraction runs and from the pair's stated recording, which a trigger enforces.
Names the recording both endpoints belong to.

Names the analysis that considered this pair. Two analyses may consider the same two detections and reach different conclusions, which is why the pair is unique within its analysis rather than globally.
Names the recording whose detections this group covers.
Names the analysis that formed this group. That analysis's groups partition every detection in its declared inputs, so a detection missing from all of them would be a defect rather than an omission.
Names the detection that belongs to the group. It must come from the analysis's declared inputs and belong to no other group of that analysis; triggers enforce both.
Names the group the detection belongs to.
Names the recording the derived interval falls in.
Names the group the interval was derived from, whose membership it repeats exactly. A derived interval whose group is removed keeps its value and loses its lineage rather than being deleted with it.
Names the analysis that derived this interval.
Names a detection the derived interval was computed from.
Names the derived interval the detection contributed to.
Names the derived interval being assessed, when the assessment targets one. Exactly one of this and the match-group reference is populated, so an assessment always has a single unambiguous subject.
Names the group being assessed, when the assessment targets one. The alternative to the consensus-event reference, never populated alongside it.
Names the analysis that produced the assessment, and through which the rule set that defined the status can be recovered.
Names the derived interval the reviewer judged, when the review targets one. One of three alternative subjects, of which exactly one is populated.
Names the correspondence the reviewer judged, when the review targets a group rather than a single detection or a derived interval.
Names the detection the reviewer judged, when the review targets one. The narrowest of the three alternative subjects.
Names the analysis the review was made in the context of. A deleted analysis leaves the review in place without it, because a human judgement outlives the run that prompted it.

Names the recording the reviewer marked the event in. The only reference this table carries: a reference event belongs to a recording and a named set, never to an analysis, so one reviewed subset can anchor comparisons across many configurations.
Names the experimental entity the aggregate was computed within, when it was scoped more narrowly than the whole analysis.

Names one endpoint of the registered feature pair a feature-level aggregate concerns. One of two references into this table, populated together with the other so the aggregate stays traceable to the exact pair it summarizes.

Names the other endpoint of that registered feature pair. Unlike the endpoints of a candidate pair or a feature relationship, these two carry no enforced ordering, so neither position implies which extractor a side came from.
Names the analysis the aggregate belongs to, ordinarily a child run of the matching analysis it summarizes.
Names the recording the composed component covers, which must belong to the agreement run's project.

Names the agreement run that composed this component. A trigger refuses a run that is not of the arbitrary-N agreement type, so a composed component cannot be attached to a pairwise matching analysis.

Names the detection belonging to the composed component. It cannot be deleted while the component holds it, which protects the member that no candidate edge joins and that would otherwise disappear without trace.
Names the composed component the detection belongs to.

Names the exact pairwise candidate edge being cited as support. It must come from a declared source analysis, describe the component's recording, and join two of its members. The cited candidate cannot be deleted while the citation stands, so a composed result never outlives its evidence.
Names the composed component the cited edge helps hold together.
Names the recording this clock belongs to when it is recording-scoped. Null leaves the clock project-scoped rather than attaching it to a recording.
Names the project in which this clock is declared, whether the clock is project-scoped or also belongs to a recording.
Names the clock whose native coordinates are used by this stream's events and coverage intervals.
Names the recording this logical stream accompanies when it is recording-scoped. Null leaves the stream scoped only to its project.
Names the project that owns this logical external stream.
Names the configuration-profile version used to interpret this source when one was registered; deletion of that version leaves the provenance row without the optional link.
Names the artifact that supplied these stream records when the provenance row is artifact-backed. Exactly one of this and the source-file reference is present.
Names the source file that supplied these stream records when the provenance row is file-backed. Exactly one of this and the artifact reference is present.
Names the logical external stream whose records came from this cited file or artifact.
Names the existing experimental entity that the source declared this event concerned, when that label resolved. This optional lookup is not visual-identity evidence.
Names the logical stream in which this event occurred and thereby identifies the event's native clock.
Names the external event that this mapped long-form attribute describes.
Names the logical stream whose observation coverage this native-clock interval asserts.
Names the artifact carrying this set's session-specific manifest when artifact-backed. At most one of the artifact and source-file manifest references is present.
Names the source file carrying this set's session-specific manifest when file-backed. At most one of the source-file and artifact manifest references is present.
Names the clock chosen as this alignment set's reference coordinate system, without asserting that its device is intrinsically more accurate.
Names the recording whose participating clocks this set aligns when the operation is recording-scoped.
Names the analysis run that owns this user-facing alignment operation and records its caller-asserted software provenance. The unique reference makes the set the run's alignment result.
Names the target reference clock in which this transform expresses values. A trigger requires it to equal the parent set's reference clock.
Names the source clock whose native coordinates this transform accepts, distinct from the target reference clock.
Names the user-facing alignment set that owns this one source-to-reference transform attempt.
Names the piecewise-affine transform attempt whose source clock carries this caller-declared breakpoint.
Names the alignment set within which this logical synchronization occurrence is identified and observed.
Names the configuration-profile version used to interpret this clock reading when one was registered; deletion leaves the observation without the optional profile link.
Names the registered source file from which this anchor reading came, when the observation is file-backed.
Names the external event that supplied this anchor reading when one exists. A trigger requires the event's stream to use the same clock as the observation.
Names the clock on which this observation read the logical anchor, independently of whether that clock is a source or reference in a particular transform.
Names the logical synchronization anchor that this one native-clock reading witnessed.
Names the existing track-to-entity association cited as identity evidence for the anchor reading. Deletion is restricted so admitted evidence cannot disappear silently.
Names the identity-dependent anchor observation qualified by this evidence link; a trigger refuses links to undeclared or device-level observations.
Names the observation on the transform's target reference clock. A trigger keeps this endpoint distinct from and correctly oriented against the source observation.
Names the observation on the transform's source clock. A trigger keeps this endpoint distinct from and correctly oriented against the reference observation.
Names the logical anchor whose source and reference observations produced this residual under the cited transform.
Names the source-to-reference transform attempt under which this anchor's prediction and residual were calculated.
Names the source-to-reference transform attempt whose authoritative coefficients this segment carries.
Names the clock in which this optional cached event interval is expressed. The transform and native timestamp remain authoritative.
Names the stored source-to-reference transform from which this optional cached interval was derived.
Names the native external event whose interval this cache projects without replacing or updating its native timestamps.
Names the declared coordinate frame for samples in this tracking stream. The declaration supplies interpretation metadata; no dense tracking samples are stored in SQLite.
Makes this row the tracking-specific extension of the same external stream. The shared key is not a second stream identity.
Names the tracking stream in which this native track and body-part series occurs. A series describes a trajectory label, not an experimental entity.
Names the exact mapping-profile version used to interpret this identity claim when profile-based mapping contributed to it.
Names the registered file from which this interval-scoped identity evidence came when it is file-backed.
Names the analysis run that produced this association when it was derived analytically; the association remains a provenance-bearing claim rather than ground truth.

Names the candidate or assigned experimental entity for the native track interval. It is null only for an unresolved association, and a non-null value remains a claim whose state and evidence must be consulted.
Names the tracking stream containing the native track to which this time-bounded identity claim applies.
Names the exact mapping-profile version used to register or interpret this acoustic reference when profile-based mapping was involved.
Names the registered file from which this reference registration came when it is file-backed.
Names the external event registered as this reference when the reference is event-backed. A trigger requires the event to belong to the same recording.
Optionally limits the reference registration to one channel of the recording. This is registration context, not a measured response.
Names the recording whose native audio-second interval contains this registered reference.
Names the consensus analysis run that supplied members when this sequence was assembled from consensus events.
Names the extraction run that supplied members when this sequence was assembled from detections.
Optionally names the experimental entity whose events form the sequence; null leaves the sequence at its broader recording or epoch scope.
Optionally scopes the sequence to one declared recording epoch.
Names the recording within which this ordered event sequence is defined.
Names the analysis run that modeled and stored this sequence.
Names the optional cached aligned projection used as this member's external-event representation; native event timing remains preserved separately.
Names the native external event occupying this sequence position when the sequence is built from external events.
Names the consensus event occupying this sequence position when the sequence is built from consensus events.
Names the extractor detection occupying this sequence position when the sequence is built from detections.
Names the ordered sequence to which this member and ordinal position belong.
Names the modeled sequence within which this bout groups a contiguous or otherwise method-defined span of members.
Names the analysis run that derived this bout boundary assignment.
Names the exact sequence member admitted to the bout and ordered within it.
Names the bout whose membership this junction row records.
Makes one bout the measurement target when the metric is evaluated at bout scope.
Makes one sequence the measurement target when the metric is evaluated at sequence scope.
Names the registry definition that supplies the measurement's metric meaning, value type, canonical unit, and allowed scope.
Names the analysis run that produced this derived value.
Makes one recording epoch the measurement target when the metric is evaluated at epoch scope.
Makes one experimental entity the measurement target when the metric is evaluated at entity scope.
Optionally qualifies the measurement with the recording channel on which it was evaluated. The channel is contextual and is not one of the mutually exclusive measurement targets.
Makes one recording the measurement target when the metric is evaluated at recording scope.
Makes one registered acoustic reference the measurement target, typically for a channel-specific response measured over that reference interval.
Makes one native external event the measurement target when the metric is evaluated for that event.
Makes one consensus event the measurement target when the metric is evaluated for the reconciled event.
Makes one extractor detection the measurement target when the metric is evaluated for that specific observation.
Names the metric definition shared by the admitted source measurements and interpreted by this channel-response aggregate.
Names the channel characterized by this estimate. The estimate is QC evidence, not a gain correction or preferred-channel designation.
Names the recording within which this channel-response estimate and every admitted source measurement were evaluated.
Names the analysis run that aggregated this channel-response estimate. A run that produces estimates is constrained to one recording.
Names the exact acoustic-reference measurement admitted as evidence for the estimate. Triggers require matching recording, channel, metric, reference type, and frequency bounds.
Names the channel-response estimate whose support population includes the cited measurement.
Names the exact settings-profile version used for this attribution attempt when one was registered, preserving its configuration independently of the method name.
Names an earlier attribution attempt from which this attempt descends when the caller declares lineage; deletion of the parent clears the optional link rather than deleting the descendant.
Names the recording whose vocal-event population this attribution attempt considers. Cross-table guards use this scope for its targets, candidates, and imported windows.
Names the analysis-run provenance record that owns this attribution attempt and records the caller-asserted software execution under which it was created.
Names the arbitrary-N agreement group targeted by this row when that is the run's event set. The row must also declare which derived group extent it uses.
Names the pairwise consensus event targeted by this row when that is the run's event set; the detection and agreement-group alternatives are then absent.
Names the extractor detection targeted by this row when the run operates on native detections; the other target references are then absent.
Names the attribution attempt whose explicit event set contains this target. A trigger requires the target event to belong to the run's recording.
Names the experimental entity being considered as a possible caller. A trigger requires an entity-to-recording link within the owning attribution run's recording.
Names the vocal-event target for which this entity is one candidate. Several candidate rows may belong to the same target, but the same entity cannot be repeated there.
Names the exact mapping-profile version that interpreted this evidence source when one was registered, answering which field and value rules were applied.
Names the registered file that supplied this evidence observation when it is file-backed, answering where the observation came from rather than what it means.
Names the exact source-to-reference clock transform used by this evidence observation when timing was projected, preserving the temporal operation it depends on.
Names the external event whose declared entity link was read when this observation rests on a declared_entity_link identity statement. This is source-declared linkage, not visual identity evidence.
Names the track-to-entity association cited when this observation rests on an identity_association statement, preserving the reviewed or explicit identity evidence actually consulted.
Names the possible caller this evidence observation concerns when it is candidate-specific. A trigger requires that candidate to belong to the row's attribution target.
Names the vocal-event target about which this evidence was observed, whether the row applies to the whole target or additionally identifies one candidate.
Names the immutable policy-profile version that produced this conclusion. Deletion is restricted so a stored decision cannot outlive the rules that make it interpretable.
Names the vocal-event target concluded by this policy-specific decision. Different policy versions may retain separate decisions for the same target.

Names one candidate selected by this decision. Insert and decision-status-update triggers require the candidate to concern the same target and check the decision status's selected-set size; direct SQL deletion can bypass the latter guarantee.
Names the policy conclusion whose selected-candidate set includes this row, allowing simultaneous conclusions to retain more than one selected caller.
Names the exact attribution-input mapping-profile version that interpreted this external window when one was registered.
Names the registered external file from which this native-clock attribution window was imported, when that provenance is available.
Names the declared native clock on which this imported window's start and end coordinates are expressed; it does not identify any later aligned projection.
Names the recording to which this external window was mapped. A trigger requires it to equal the owning attribution run's recording.
Names the imported-path attribution attempt that received this external window and scopes its source-native window identity.
Names the canonical entity to which the external caller label resolved under declared mapping rules, when resolution occurred. A trigger requires the entity to belong to the run's recording.
Names the external vocalization window over which this source caller assertion was made. The relationship does not promote the claim to a VAWLUME candidate.
Names the exact clock-transform attempt used to project this imported window when the correspondence's IoU basis is aligned.
Names the VAWLUME vocal-event target compared with the imported window. Several correspondences may name competing targets, preserving ambiguity rather than selecting one.
Names the external native-clock window compared with the VAWLUME target. A trigger requires both sides of the correspondence to belong to the same attribution run.
